title: Modular child care to expand affordable spaces
subtitle: A delegate sought more funded child care spaces, and public health information on overdoses was requested.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that the Region borrow up to $4.4M in debentures to buy up to two 88-space modular child care centres {{vote:m1}}. They would be placed on Waterloo Region District School Board land in priority neighbourhoods and leased affordably to not-for-profit operators.

Staff said the project would not increase the tax levy, because operators would repay the Region with interest. The funding must be allocated and communicated to the Ministry of Health by the end of October, so it could not wait for the 2026 budget. Staff reported more than 8,000 children are waiting for care immediately. Council still has to adopt the recommendation.

A delegate from a Kitchener child care centre asked the Region to use unallocated funded spaces and to press the province for more. In other business, the Medical Officer of Health agreed to share public health information on drug addictions and overdoses with the committee.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing up to $4.4M in debentures to buy up to two 88-space modular child care centres, to be repaid through long-term affordable leases to not-for-profit operators {{vote:m1}}.

The committee recommended authorizing the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services to sign affordable leases with operators chosen through an application process, on terms satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
The committee recommended authorizing the Commissioner of Community Services to sign a lease with the Waterloo Region District School Board to prepare the land for modular child care.

debate: Staff said not-for-profit operators struggle to find affordable, suitable sites, with high rents, little green space and costly renovations. School properties offer accessibility, green space, no zoning concerns and minimal site costs.

One councillor asked why such a large request was coming outside the budget process. Staff replied that all costs would be repaid by operators with interest and a small admin fee, so the levy would not rise. They also pointed to the end-of-October deadline to commit the funding to the Ministry.

One councillor asked whether leasing space to operators is a normal Regional role. Staff said it falls outside the Region's usual service system manager role. They judged it appropriate given community need, since market leases of five to ten years are too short for operators to afford.

A delegate from a Kitchener child care centre said the region received too few funded spaces for its growth. The delegate said many families on the centre's waitlist cannot afford unfunded fees, and asked the Region to use unused spaces and lobby the province.
One councillor asked for a later-in-year update on overdoses and ambulance calls, to learn the impact of losing the safe injection site.
